pairs.why: A's boot has a normal shaft with the spur strap wrapped around the heel, while B's shaft is an odd tall stovepipe with a seam that doesn't sit naturally on the foot.
Both chess tables have boards that lie flat in perspective, pedestals that sit on plinths and stools that rest on the grass, so I see no clear building error in either.
B's life ring hangs from a hook on the post and the deck runs back cleanly between its pilings, while A's rope runs oddly from the life ring to the coiled post, so the ring hangs from nothing.
A reads as a wall clock seen straight on, while B's round clock stands on a floor on its curved rim with no stand or base to hold it up.
B's labelled keys sit in rows that follow the tilted face, while A's keypad is a grid of blank buttons, so the calculator couldn't be used.
A's cat sits naturally on a flat floor, while B's floor tilts steeply under a stiff body with a tube-like collar and a thick looped tail that don't match the camera.
A's life ring hangs from a peg on the front post of a pier that is built consistently, while B's ring floats near a post and its reflection appears far away from it in the water.
The two wagons are almost identical, with the same wheel sizes, axles, cover and tongue, so neither is built more correctly.
